1. If the answer is "yes," at least 1/2 of computation paths accept.
2. If the answer is "no," fewer than 1/2 of computation paths accept.

Defined in {ref:gil77}. PP is closed under union and intersection {ref:brs91} (open for 14 years). More generally, P^{PP[log]} = PP; PP is closed under polynomial-time truth-table reductions.

Contains P^{NP[log]} {ref:bhw89} and QMA {ref:mw05}. BPP, BQP, and YQP* are all low for PP {ref:kst89b} {ref:fr98} {ref:yir24}. PH ⊆ P^PP {ref:tod89}.

Equals PostBQP {ref:aar05b}. Equals PQP {ref:wat09}.

For any fixed k, PP contains a language without circuits of size n^k {ref:vin04b}; even without quantum circuits of size n^k with quantum advice {ref:aar06}.

name: PPSPACE
desc: Same as IPP, except that IPP uses private coins while PPSPACE uses public coins.

name: PP/poly
desc: Contains BQP/qpoly {ref:aar04b}.

name: PQP
desc: The class of decision problems solvable in polynomial time by a quantum Turing machine, with less than 1/2 probability of error.

name: PQUERY
desc: The class of decision problems solvable in polynomial space using at most a polynomial number of queries to the oracle.

name: PR
desc:
Primitive Recursive Functions. The class of functions definable by recursively building up arithmetic operations: addition, multiplication, exponentiation, tetration, etc. What is NOT allowed is to diagonalize over a whole series of such functions to produce an even faster-growing one.

The Ackermann function (proposed 1928) is an example of a recursive function that is NOT primitive recursive, showing PR ⊊ R.

Alternatively, PR is exactly the class computable by programs in an idealized ALGOL-like language where only definite loops are allowed (loops where the number of iterations is specified before the loop begins).

Strictly contains {lang:ELEMENTARY}. Does not have complete problems under elementary reductions (unlike {lang:TOWER} and {lang:Ack}).

name: PSK
desc: Yeah, I'm told that's what the S and K stand for.

name: PSPACE
desc: Polynomial space. Problems decided in polynomial space by a deterministic Turing machine.

name: PSPACE/poly
desc: Contains QMA/qpoly {ref:aar06b}.

name: PT_1
desc: The class of Boolean functions f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} such that f(x)=sgn(p(x)), where p is a polynomial having a number of terms polynomial in n.

name: PZK
desc: Perfect Zero Knowledge. A promise problem is in PZK if there exists an interactive proof system (a polynomial-time probabilistic verifier interacting with a polynomial-time prover) such that: (1) For YES instances, there exists a polynomial-time prover that causes the verifier to accept with high probability; (2) For NO instances, for any prover, the verifier accepts with low probability; (3) For YES instances, there exists a polynomial-time simulator that, given only the input, can generate a transcript whose distribution is identically (not just statistically) distributed as the verifier's view in the real protocol. That is, the verifier learns nothing beyond the validity of the statement, and the simulation is perfect (the distributions are exactly equal, not just close).

name: P^K
desc: P equipped with an oracle that, given a string x, returns the length of the shortest program that outputs x.

name: P^NP
desc: P With NP Oracle. See {lang:Delta_2P}.

name: P^NP[k]
desc:
P With k NP Queries (for constant k). Equals P with 2^k - 1 parallel queries to NP (i.e., queries that do not depend on prior answers) {ref:bh91} {ref:hem89}.

If P^{NP[1]} = P^{NP[2]}, then P^{NP[1]} = P^{NP[log]} and PH collapses to Δ_3P (Kadin; attributed in {ref:har87b}).

name: P^NP[log]
desc:
P With O(log n) NP Queries. Also known as Θ_2P. The class of decision problems solvable by a P machine making O(log n) queries to an NP oracle.

Equals P^{||NP} (P with polynomially many nonadaptive NP queries) {ref:bh91} {ref:hem89}. Contained in {lang:PP} {ref:bhw89}. Contains P^{NP[k]} for all constants k.

Determining the winner of Dodgson's 1876 election system is P^{NP[log]}-complete {ref:hhr97}.

name: P^NP[log^2]
desc: Same as [[#pnplog|P^NP[log]]], except that now log^2 queries can be made.

name: P^PP
desc: A level of the counting hierarchy CH.

name: P^QMA[log]
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a P machine, that can make O(log n) queries to a QMA oracle (where n is the length of the input).

name: P^#P
desc: I decided this class is so important that it deserves an entry of its own, apart from #P.

name: P^SharpP[1]
desc: P With a Single #P Query. Contains {lang:PH} {ref:tod89}. Indeed, contains {lang:MP}, which in turn contains {lang:ModPH} {ref:gkr95}.

name: P^||NP
desc: Equals [[#pnplog|P^NP[log]]] ({ref:bh91} and {ref:hem89} independently).

name: P^||QMA
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a P machine that can make a polynomial number of non-adaptive queries to a QMA oracle.

name: P_CTC
desc: Same as P with access to bits along a closed time curve.

name: P/log
desc: Same as P/poly, except that the advice string for input size n can have length at most logarithmic in n, rather than polynomial.

name: P/poly
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of polynomial-size Boolean circuits.

name: ⊕EXP
desc:
Parity EXP. The exponential-time analogue of ⊕P.

There exists an oracle relative to which ⊕EXP = ZPP {ref:bbf98}.

name: ⊕L
desc:
Parity L. Has the same relation to L as ⊕P does to P: the class of decision problems solvable by an NL machine such that the answer is "yes" iff the number of accepting paths is odd.

Contains {lang:SL} {ref:kw93}.

Solving a linear system over Z_2 is ⊕L-complete {ref:dam90}. Simulating stabilizer circuits is ⊕L-complete {ref:ag04}.

⊕L^{⊕L} = ⊕L {ref:bdh92} {ref:hrv00}.

name: ⊕L/poly
desc: Nonuniform ⊕L. Has the same relation to ⊕L as P/poly does to P.

name: ⊕P
desc:
Parity P. The class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine such that:
1. If the answer is "yes," the number of accepting paths is odd.
2. If the answer is "no," the number of accepting paths is even.

Defined in {ref:pz83}.

Contains Graph Isomorphism; indeed, Graph Isomorphism is low for ⊕P {ref:ak02}. Contains {lang:FewP} {ref:ch89}.

There exists an oracle where P = ⊕P but P ≠ NP (and NP = EXP) {ref:bbf98}.

Equals Mod_{2^m}P for every positive integer m.

name: ⊕P^cc
desc:
Communication Complexity ⊕P. The communication complexity analog of ⊕P.

Not contained in UPP^cc {ref:for02}. Does not contain ZPP^cc if partial functions are allowed {ref:gpw16b}.

The complexity measure associated with ⊕P^cc is equivalent to the log of the rank of the communication matrix over GF(2).

name: ⊕SAC^0
desc: AC^0 With Unbounded Parity Gates. Constant-depth circuits with unbounded-fanin XOR and bounded-fanin AND gates, along with NOT gates at input level. The "parity" analog of AC^0.

name: ⊕SAC^1
desc: The class of problems solvable by a nonuniform family of polynomial-size, polylog-depth circuits with unbounded-fanin XOR and bounded-fanin AND gates.

name: PermUP
desc: The class of languages L in UP such that the mapping from an input x to the unique witness for x is a permutation of L.

name: PhP
desc: Defined by Valiant {ref:val03} to be "the class of physically constructible polynomial resource computers" (characterizing what "can be computed in the physical world in practice").

name: Φ_2P
desc:
Second Level of the Symmetric Hierarchy (Alternative Definition). The class of problems for which there exists a polynomial-time predicate P(x,y,z) such that for all x, if the answer on input x is "yes," then:
1. For all y, there exists a z for which P(x,y,z).
2. For all z, there exists a y for which P(x,y,z).

Contained in {lang:Sigma_2P} and {lang:Pi_2P}.

Defined in {ref:can96}, where it was also observed that Φ_2P = {lang:S_2P}.

name: Π_2P
desc:
Universal polynomial time, 2 alternations. coNP^NP, the second universal level of the polynomial hierarchy PH. A language L is in Π_2P if there is a polynomial-time predicate R such that x ∈ L iff ∀y ∃z R(x,y,z). Complement of Σ_2P.

BPP ⊆ Σ_2P ∩ Π_2P {ref:lau83}. AM ⊆ Π_2P.

name: PostBPP
desc: Alias for BPP_path.

name: PostBQP
desc: A class inspired by the proverb, "if at first you don't succeed, try, try again."

name: PrSPACE(f(n))
desc: Has the same relation to DSPACE(f(n)) as PP does to P.

name: Pr_HSPACE(f(n))
desc: Has the same relation to DSPACE(f(n)) as PP does to P.

name: PromiseP
desc: The class of promise problems solvable by a P machine.

name: PromiseUP
desc: The class of promise problems solvable by an UP machine.

name: PureSuperQMA
desc: Same as QMA, except now the witness is a pure state, and the verifier can directly obtain the probability that any one of a polynomial number of observables of the witness, if measured, would equal 1.

name: QAC
desc: Quantum AC. The class of decision problems solvable by polylogarithmic-depth, polynomial-size uniform quantum circuit. Here each layer of the circuit is a tensor product of one-qubit gates and Toffoli gates, or is a tensor product of controlled-NOT gates. Quantum generalization of AC^0. Quantum generalization of AC.

name: QACC^0
desc: Same as QAC^0[m], except that Mod-m gates are allowed for any m.

name: QAC^0
desc: Quantum AC^0. The class of decision problems solvable by constant-depth, polynomial-size uniform quantum circuit. Here each layer of the circuit is a tensor product of one-qubit gates and Toffoli gates, or is a tensor product of controlled-NOT gates. Quantum generalization of AC^0. It's unknown whether it contains AC^0.

name: QAC_f^0
desc: Same as QAC^0, except that an additional "quantum fanout" gate is available, which CNOT's a qubit into arbitrarily many target qubits in a single step.

name: QAM
desc: Quantum Arthur-Merlin. Like {lang:AM}, but Merlin's proof is a quantum state and the verifier is a BQP machine; like {lang:QMA}, but there can be a classical random challenge string first.

name: QCFL
desc: The class of decision problems recognized by quantum context-free languages, which are defined in {ref:mc00}.

name: QCMA
desc: Quantum-Classical Merlin-Arthur. Like {lang:QMA}, but Merlin's proof is a classical string; like NP, but the verifier has a quantum computer (a {lang:BQP} machine).

name: QCPH
desc:
Quantum Classical Polynomial Hierarchy. A bounded-error quantum generalization of {lang:PH} in which all proofs are classical and the verifier is a quantum circuit.

Defined in {ref:gsssy18}. Contained in P^{PP^{PP}} {ref:gsssy18}. Contains {lang:PH} and is contained in {lang:QPH} {ref:gy24}.

name: QEPH
desc: Like QPH, but the provers may entangle their earlier proofs with their later proofs.

name: QH
desc: QH_k is defined to be P^NP[k]; that is, P with k queries to an NP oracle (where k is a constant).

name: QIP
desc:
Quantum Interactive Proof Systems. Like {lang:IP}, but the verifier is a BQP (quantum polynomial-time) algorithm, and messages can be quantum states. The prover has unbounded resources (but obeys quantum mechanics). The verifier and prover may become entangled.

Defined in {ref:wat99}, where PSPACE ⊆ QIP[3] was shown. KW00 showed that for k > 3, QIP[k] = QIP[3] = QIP. QIP ⊆ EXP {ref:kw00}.

QIP = IP = PSPACE {ref:jjuw09}; quantum computing adds no power to single-prover interactive proofs.

QIP(1) is known as {lang:QMA}.

name: QIP[2]
desc: Quantum Interactive Proofs with 2 rounds, a restricted form {lang:QIP}. Compare with the note on {lang:AM} about restricted rounds. It turns out that QIP[k>=3]=QIP[3]=QIP, and QIP[1] is by definition QMA, so the only other interesting case is QIP[2].

name: QL
desc: The class of problems that can be decided in quasi-linear time by a multitape deterministic Turing machine.

name: QMA-plus
desc: Same as QMA, except now the verifier can directly obtain the probability that a given observable of the certificate state, if measured, would equal 1.

name: QMA
desc: Quantum Merlin-Arthur. Problems for which an omniscient 'Merlin' can submit a proof to 'Arthur' that a statement is true, and Arthur believes it with high probability (<1/3 chance of failing) -- but this proof can be a quantum state, and Arthur has a quantum computer.

name: QMAM
desc: The class of decision problems for which a "yes" answer can be verified by a public-coin quantum MAM protocol, as follows.

name: QMA^+
desc: Same as QMA, except now the witness must contain a state with non-negative amplitudes in the computational basis.

name: QMA^+(2)
desc: Same as QMA(2), except now *each* witness must contain a state with non-negative amplitudes in the computational basis.

name: QMA_1
desc: Same as QMA except that for a "yes" instance, there exists a state that is accepted with probability 1.

name: QMA(2)
desc: Same as QMA, except that now the verifier is given two polynomial-size quantum certificates, which are guaranteed to be unentangled.

name: QMA_log
desc: Same as QMA except that the quantum proof has O(log n) qubits instead of a polynomial number.

name: QMA/qpoly
desc: QMA With Polynomial-Size Quantum Advice. Contained in {lang:PSPACE/poly} {ref:aar06b}.

name: QMIP
desc: The quantum generalization of MIP, and the multi-prover generalization of QIP.

name: QMIP_le
desc: Same as QMIP, except that now the provers share only a polynomial number of EPR pairs, instead of an unlimited number.

name: QMIP_ne
desc: Same as QMIP, except that now the provers have no prior entanglement.

name: QNC
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by polylogarithmic-depth quantum circuits with bounded probability of error. The zoo says, "A uniformity condition may also be imposed."; for the purpose of this site we _do_ impose that condition. Some sources like https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3570637 refer to this as BQNC.

name: QNC^0
desc:
Quantum NC^0. Constant-depth quantum circuits without fanout gates. (A uniformity condition may also be imposed.)

Defined in {ref:spa02}. Contained in {lang:QNC_f^0}.

name: QNC^0/qpoly
desc: Constant-depth quantum circuits with bounded fan-in, with polynomial size quantum advice.

name: QNC^0/🐱
desc:
Quantum NC^0 With Polynomial-Size Quantum Cat-State Advice. Constant-depth quantum circuits without fanout gates, with an additional cat state as "advice": 🐱 = (|0^n⟩ + |1^n⟩)/√2.

Defined in {ref:wkst19}. Contains {lang:QNC^0}. Contained in {lang:QNC^0_qpoly} and BQP.

name: QNC^1
desc:
Quantum NC^1. The class of decision problems solvable by logarithmic-depth bounded-error quantum circuits. (A uniformity condition may also be imposed.)

See {lang:QNC} for context. In contrast to {lang:NC^1}, it is not clear how to simulate QNC^1 on a quantum computer with one pure qubit and the rest maximally mixed {ref:asv00}.

name: QNC_f^0
desc: Constant-depth quantum circuits with unbounded-fanout gates.

name: QP
desc: Equals DTIME(2^polylog(n)).

name: QPH
desc: A bounded-error quantum generalization of PH in which all proofs are un-entangled mixed quantum states, and the verifier is a quantum circuit.

name: QPIP
desc: Like IP, but the prover is a BQP machine, not unbounded.

name: QPLIN
desc: Equals DTIME(n^O(log n)).

name: QPSPACE
desc: Equals DSPACE(2^polylog(n)).

name: QRG
desc: Same as RG, except that now the verifier is a BQP machine, and can exchange polynomially many quantum messages with the competing provers.

name: QRG(1)
desc: The class of problems for which there exists a BQP machine M such that:

name: QRG(2)
desc: Same as QRG, except that now the verifier can exchange only two messages with each prover.

name: QRG(k)
desc: Same as QRG, except that now the verifier exchanges exactly k messages with each prover where k is a polynomial-bounded function of the input length.

name: QRL
desc: The class of problems nondeterministically recognized by Moore-Crutchfield Quantum Finite Automata.

name: QSZK
desc:
Quantum Statistical Zero-Knowledge. A quantum analog of HVSZK. The verifier is a BQP algorithm who can exchange quantum messages with Merlin; their states may become entangled. The zero-knowledge requirement: each mixed state in Arthur's view must have trace distance ≤ 1/10 from a state Arthur could prepare himself (in BQP), without help.

Defined in {ref:wat02}, where it was shown that:
- QSZK ⊆ PSPACE.
- QSZK is closed under complement.
- Any protocol can be parallelized to two messages; QSZK ⊆ QIP[2].
- Protocols can be assumed public-coin (as for SZK).
- Complete promise problem: Quantum State Distinguishability (QSD) — given circuits Q_0, Q_1 producing states ρ_0, ρ_1, decide whether their trace distance is ≤ α or ≥ β (where α < β²).

Honest-verifier QSZK equals general-verifier QSZK {ref:wat09b}. There exist oracles relative to which QSZK does not contain UP ∩ coUP or UP {ref:mw18}.

name: R
desc:
Recursive Languages. The class of decision problems solvable by a Turing machine. Often identified with the class of effectively computable functions (the Church-Turing thesis).

Defined in {ref:tur36} {ref:chu41} and other seminal early papers.

Equals RE ∩ coRE. Strictly contains {lang:PR} (the primitive recursive functions) {ref:kle71}.

name: RBQP
desc:
Strict Quantum RP. The class of problems in NP whose witnesses are in FBQP. For example, the set of square-free numbers is in coRBQP using only the fact that factoring is in FBQP (the factorization proves there is a square divisor, even without proving the factors are prime).

Contains {lang:RP} and {lang:ZBQP}. Contained in {lang:BQP} and {lang:RQP}.

Defined here to clarify {lang:EQP}; see also {lang:ZBQP}.

name: RE
desc:
Recursively Enumerable Languages. The class of decision problems for which a "yes" answer can be verified by a Turing machine in a finite amount of time. (If the answer is "no," the machine might never halt.)

Equivalently, the class of decision problems for which a Turing machine can list all "yes" instances one by one ("enumerable").

The canonical RE-complete problem is the Halting Problem. A problem is complete for RE under M-reductions (many-one Turing reductions) or T-reductions (Turing reductions); these give different complete sets.

Complement of {lang:coRE}.

name: REG
desc:
Regular Languages. The class of decision problems solvable by deterministic finite automata (DFAs), equivalently nondeterministic finite automata (NDFAs).

Equals DSPACE(O(1)) {ref:she59}, which equals DSPACE(o(log log n)) {ref:hls65}.

Can recognize "Is the parity of the input odd?" but not "Are the majority of bits in the input 1's?" (finite automata cannot count).

Contained in {lang:NC^1}.

name: RG
desc: The class of problems solvable by a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier who can exchange a polynomial number of messages with two competing, computationally-unbounded provers -- one trying to convince the verifier that the answer is "yes," the other that the answer is "no." Note that the verif...

name: RG(1)
desc: The class of problems for which there exists a BPP machine M such that, on input x:

name: RG(2)
desc: Same as RG, except that now the verifier can exchange only two messages with each prover.

name: RG(k)
desc: Same as RG, except that now the verifier exchanges exactly k messages with each prover where k is a polynomial-bounded function of the input length.

name: RL
desc:
Randomized Logspace. Has the same relation to L as RP does to P. The randomized machine must halt with probability 1 on any input and also run in polynomial time (otherwise we'd just get NL).

Contains R_H L. Contained in SC {ref:nis92}.

{ref:rtv05} give strong evidence that RL = L.

name: RNC
desc:
Randomized Nick's Class. The class of decision problems solvable by polylogarithmic-depth polynomial-size random circuits with bounded one-sided error: it must never incorrectly accept (no false positives), and it must accept correctly with probability at least 1/2 (for "yes" inputs).

Analogous to how RP relates to P. Contains perfect matching (Schwartz-Zippel; Mulmuley-Vazirani-Vazirani algorithm).

name: RNC^0
desc: Randomized constant-depth circuits of bounded-fanin. Not very interesting because the randomness cannot be useful, so this is equal to NC^0. But the functional version FRNC^0 is slightly more interesting (in the same way that FNC^0 is more interesting than NC^0) and has been used in reductions, e.g. https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2023/17506/pdf/LIPIcs-ITCS-2023-3.pdf

name: RNC^1
desc: Randomized log-depth circuits of bounded-fanin.

name: RP
desc:
Randomized Polynomial-Time. The class of decision problems solvable by a probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine such that:
1. If the answer is "yes," at least 1/2 of computation paths accept.
2. If the answer is "no," all computation paths reject.

Defined in {ref:gil77}. Contains primality testing {ref:ah87}, though primality is now known to be in P {ref:aks02}.

ZPP = RP ∩ coRP. RP and ZPP have the same p-measure (either zero or one); if nonzero, then ZPP = BPP = EXP {ref:im03}.

See also: {lang:coRP}, {lang:ZPP}, {lang:BPP}.

name: RPP
desc: The class of decision problems (x,m) (where x is an input of length |x|=n and m is an integer parameter), that are solvable by a nondeterministic (i.e.

name: RQP
desc:
One-Sided Randomized Quantum Polynomial-Time. The class of problems solvable by a QTM that:
1. Accepts with probability 0 when the answer is "no."
2. Accepts with probability at least 1/2 when the answer is "yes."

The quantum analog of RP. Since one acceptance probability must exactly vanish, RQP has the same technical caveats as {lang:EQP}. Complement is {lang:coRQP}. ZQP = RQP ∩ coRQP.

name: RSPACE(f(n))
desc: Same as RL, but for O(f(n))-space instead of logarithmic-space.

name: R_HL
desc: Has the same relation to L as RP does to P.

name: R_HSPACE(f(n))
desc: Has the same relation to BP_HSPACE(f(n)) as RP does to BPP.

name: RevSPACE(f(n))
desc: The class of decision problems solvable in space O(f(n)) by a reversible Turing machine (a deterministic Turing machine for which every configuration has at most one immediate predecessor).

name: S_2P
desc:
Second Level of the Symmetric Hierarchy. The class of problems for which there is a polynomial-time predicate P such that, on input x:
1. If the answer is "yes," then there exists a y such that for all z, P(x,y,z) is true.
2. If the answer is "no," then there exists a z such that for all y, P(x,y,z) is false.

The definition is symmetric: the prover and disprover submit simultaneous moves to a referee. Contrast with {lang:Sigma_2P}, where the prover moves first.

Defined independently in {ref:rs98} and {ref:can96}. Contains {lang:MA} and Δ_2P {ref:rs98}. Contained in ZPP^NP {ref:cai01}.

Φ_2P = S_2P (alternate definition) {ref:can96}. Also written symP. If NP ⊆ P/poly then PH = S_2P (Sengupta; see {ref:cai01}), and even PH = O_2P {ref:cr06}.

name: SAC
desc:
Semi-Unbounded-Fanin AC. SAC^k is the class of decision problems solvable by a family of depth-O(log^k n) circuits with unbounded-fanin OR gates and bounded-fanin (fan-in 2) AND gates. Negations are only allowed at the input level. A uniformity condition may also be imposed.

Defined in {ref:bcd89}, where it was shown SAC^k is closed under complement for every k > 0.

See {lang:SAC^0} and {lang:SAC^1} for specific levels.

name: SAC^0
desc:
Semi-Unbounded-Fanin AC^0. SAC^k is the class of decision problems solvable by a family of depth-O(log^k n) circuits with unbounded-fanin OR gates and bounded-fanin (fan-in 2) AND gates. Negations are allowed only at the input level. A uniformity condition may also be imposed. SAC^k sits "halfway" between NC^k and AC^k.

SAC^0 strictly contains NC^0 and is strictly contained in AC^0. Under standard uniformity, SAC^0 = NC^1.

name: SAC^1
desc: Semi-Unbounded-Fanin AC^1. See {lang:SAC^0} for the definition of SAC^k. SAC^1 (with a uniformity condition) contains CFL (context-free languages) and NL. Contained in AC^1 and NC^2.

name: SAPTIME
desc:
Stochastic Alternating Polynomial-Time. The class of problems solvable by a polynomial-time Turing machine with three kinds of quantifiers: existential, universal, and randomized.

Defined in {ref:pap83}, where it was also observed that SAPTIME = PSPACE.

name: SBP
desc:
Small Bounded-Error Probability. The class of decision problems for which the following holds: there exists a #P function f and an FP function g such that, for all inputs x:
1. If the answer is "yes," f(x) > g(x).
2. If the answer is "no," f(x) < g(x)/2.

Defined in {ref:bgm02}, where it was also shown that:
- SBP contains {lang:MA}, WAPP, and {lang:ExistsBPP}.
- SBP is contained in {lang:AM} and BPP_path.
- SBP is closed under union.
- There exists an oracle relative to which SBP ⊄ Σ_2P.

There exists an oracle relative to which SBP is not closed under intersection {ref:glm15}.

If SAT can be solved by an NP-machine with a subexponential number of accepting paths, then SBP = AM {ref:vol20}.

name: SBQP
desc:
Small Bounded-Error Quantum Polynomial-Time. The class of decision problems for which there exists a polynomial-time quantum algorithm that accepts with probability at least 2^{-p(n)} if the answer is "yes," and with probability at most 2^{-p(n)-1} if the answer is "no," for some polynomial p.

Defined by Kuperberg {ref:kup09}, where it was shown that SBQP = {lang:A_0PP}.

name: SC
desc:
Steve's Class (named in honor of Stephen Cook). The class of decision problems solvable by a Turing machine that simultaneously uses polynomial time and polylogarithmic space.

Note that SC might be smaller than P ∩ polyL, since for polyL it only requires a single polylogarithmic-space algorithm, while SC requires one algorithm that is both simultaneously polynomial-time and polylogarithmic-space.

Deterministic context-free languages (DCFLs) can be recognized in SC {ref:coo79}. Contains {lang:RL} and {lang:BPL} {ref:nis92}. Equals DTISP(poly, polylog).

name: SE
desc:
Subexponentially-Solvable Search Problems. The class of FNP search problems solvable in O(2^{εn}) time for every ε > 0.

Defined in {ref:ipz01}, where reductions were given showing that if any of k-SAT, k-colorability, k-set cover, clique, or vertex cover is in SE, then all of them are.

name: SEH
desc: The union of NE, NP^NE, NP^NP^NE, and so on.

name: SF
desc: Star-free languages, see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star-free_language. A subset of regular languages, where constant terms are allowed, and then we take the closure under complementation, union, and concatenation. Intersection comes for free. For example, the regex (ab)* is in this class, but (aa)* is not.

name: SF_k
desc:
Width-k Bottleneck Turing Machines. The class of decision problems solvable by a k-bottleneck Turing machine: a machine that, after a polynomial amount of time, erases everything on the tape except for a single k-valued "safe-storage." There is also a counter recording the number of erasings, which acts as a nondeterministic witness. For example, SF_2 contains both ⊕P and NP by using the counter as a witness.

Defined in {ref:cf91}, where it was also shown that SF_5 = PSPACE.

The complexity of SF_2, SF_3, and SF_4 was studied in {ref:ogi94} and {ref:her97}. Among the results: SF_4 ⊆ BP·⊕P^{Mod_3P^{⊕P^{Mod_3P^{⊕P}}}}.

name: SKC
desc: A hierarchy of generalizations of SZK, in which Arthur is allowed to gain some information from his interaction with Merlin.

name: SL
desc:
Symmetric Logarithmic-Space. The class of problems solvable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in logarithmic space, such that:
1. If the answer is "yes," one or more computation paths accept.
2. If the answer is "no," all paths reject.
3. If the machine can make a nondeterministic transition from configuration A to configuration B, then it can also transition from B to A. (This is what "symmetric" means.)

Defined in {ref:lp82}.

The undirected s-t connectivity problem (USTCON: is there a path from vertex s to vertex t in an undirected graph?) is complete for SL under L-reductions.

SL contains {lang:L} and is contained in {lang:NL}. Contained in L/poly {ref:akl79}. Contained in ⊕L and Mod_kL for every prime k {ref:kw93}. Contained in DSPACE(log^{3/2} n) {ref:nsw92} and DSPACE(log^{4/3} n) {ref:atw00}.

SL = coSL, and SL^SL = SL (the symmetric logspace hierarchy collapses) {ref:nt95}.

Reingold ultimately showed SL = L {ref:rei04}, even relative to an oracle.

name: SLICEWISE PSPACE
desc: The parameterized version of PSPACE.

name: SNP
desc:
Strict NP. {ref:fag74} showed that NP is precisely the class of decision problems reducible to a graph-theoretic property expressible in second-order existential logic.

SNP is the class of decision problems reducible to a graph-theoretic predicate with only universal quantifiers over vertices and no existential quantifiers. As an example, k-SAT (CNF satisfiability with at most k literals per clause, for k a constant) is in SNP. General SAT is not in SNP, because we need to say "there exists a literal in this clause that satisfies the clause."

Contains {lang:MMSNP}. See also {lang:MaxSNP}.

name: SO
desc:
Second-Order Logic. An extension of First-Order Logic ({lang:FO}) with quantification over second-order variables (which represent sets or relations of arbitrary arity).

Formulae can be put into prenex normal form: all second-order quantifiers first, followed by a first-order formula. SO is equal to {lang:PH} (the polynomial hierarchy) {ref:imm98}. More precisely, SO formulae in prenex normal form with k alternating second-order quantifiers correspond to the k-th level of PH. SO with only existential second-order quantification equals Σ_1 = NP {ref:fag74}, and with only universal quantification equals Π_1 = coNP.

See also: {lang:SO(Horn)}, {lang:SO(Krom)}, {lang:SO[LFP]}, {lang:SO[TC]}, and {lang:HO}.

name: SP
desc:
Semi-Efficient Parallel. The class of problems in P for which the best parallel algorithm (using a polynomial number of processors) is faster than the best serial algorithm by a factor of Ω(n^ε) for some ε > 0.

Defined in {ref:krs90}.

SP is also an alternate name for {lang:XP_uniform}.

name: SPARSE
desc: The class of decision problems for which the number of 'yes' instances of size n is upper-bounded by a polynomial in n.

name: SPL
desc:
Stoic PL. Has the same relation to {lang:PL} as SPP does to PP: an NL machine where the number of accepting paths differs by 1 (yes vs. no cases).

Contains {lang:UL}. Contained in {lang:C_eqL} and Mod_kL.

Contains the maximum matching and perfect matching problems under a pseudorandom assumption {ref:arz99}.

Equals the set of problems low for {lang:GapL}.

name: SPP
desc:
Stoic PP. The class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine such that:
1. If the answer is "no," the number of accepting paths equals the number of rejecting paths.
2. If the answer is "yes," these numbers differ by exactly 1 (or, in the all-paths-equal variant, by 2).

Defined in {ref:ffk94}, where it was shown that SPP is low for PP, C_=P, Mod_kP, and SPP itself (adding SPP as oracle does not increase their power). Independently defined in {ref:oh93} (called XP there).

Contained in {lang:LWPP}, C_=P, and {lang:WPP}. Contains {lang:FewP}; FewP is low for SPP.

Contains the problem of deciding if a graph has any nontrivial automorphisms {ref:kst92}. Contains Graph Isomorphism {ref:ak02}. Contains many problems for solvable black-box groups: solvability, membership, subgroup testing, order, nilpotence, group isomorphism, and intersection {ref:vin04}. The Hidden Subgroup Problem for permutation groups is in FP^SPP {ref:ak02}.

name: SQG
desc: Same as QRG(2), except that now the verifier can process the yes-prover's answer before preparing the no-prover's question.

name: SUBEXP
desc: Deterministic Subexponential-Time. The intersection of DTIME(2^{n^ε}) over all ε > 0. Note that the algorithm used may vary with ε.

name: SZK
desc:
Statistical Zero Knowledge. The class of decision problems where a "yes" answer can be verified by a statistical zero-knowledge proof protocol: a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier exchanges messages with an unbounded prover, and becomes convinced of "yes" without learning anything else (statistically).

Formally: for each verifier choice of random coins, its "view" of the interaction must be statistically close (trace distance ≤ 1/10) to a distribution the verifier could generate alone (in polynomial time), without the prover.

Graph non-isomorphism is a famous example in SZK. Defined in {ref:gmr89} (for zero-knowledge in general).

SZK is closed under complement {ref:oka96}. Can be assumed constant-round and public-coin {ref:oka96}. Complete promise problem: Statistical Difference (SD) {ref:sv97}. Another complete: Entropy Difference (ED) {ref:gv99}.

Contains {lang:PZK} and {lang:NISZK}. Contained in AM ∩ coAM and {lang:CZK} and {lang:QSZK}.

If any hard-on-average language is in SZK, one-way functions exist {ref:ost91}. There exists an oracle where SZK ⊄ BQP {ref:aar02}. Contained in {lang:DQP} {ref:aar02b}.

name: SZK_h
desc:
SZK With Limited Help. The class of decision problems for which a "yes" answer can be verified by a statistical zero-knowledge proof protocol, and the prover and verifier both have access to a string computed by a trusted probabilistic polynomial-time third party with access to the input.

Defined in {ref:bg03}, where it was also shown that SZK_h = {lang:SZK}.

Contains {lang:NISZK_h}.

name: S^≠
desc:
Exclusive Stochastic Languages. The class of languages L for which there is a real number p and a probabilistic finite automaton M such that:
- If x ∈ L, then M accepts x with some probability not exactly equal to p.
- If x ∉ L, then M accepts x with probability exactly equal to p.

Shown that S^≠ = NQL (Nondeterministic Quantum Languages) {ref:yak10}.

name: S_2-EXP•P^NP
desc: One of the caged classes of the Complexity Zoo.

name: S_2E
desc: Same as S_2P, except that the predicate P may be exponential.

name: SelfNP
desc: The class of languages L in NP such that the union, over all x in L, of the set of valid witnesses for x equals L itself.

name: Sigma_2P
desc:
The second existential level of the Polynomial Hierarchy. NP^NP: problems solvable by NP with an NP oracle. A language L is in Σ_2P if there is a polynomial-time predicate R such that x ∈ L iff ∃y ∀z R(x,y,z).

Contains NP and coNP^NP. If BPP ⊄ Σ_2P then NP ≠ BPP. BPP ⊆ Σ_2P ∩ Π_2P {ref:lau83}.

Σ_2P-complete: minimum circuit size (MCSP) with NP oracle, Succinct SAT.

See {lang:PH} for context.

name: StoqMA
desc:
Stoquastic Merlin-Arthur. The class of decision problems solvable by a Merlin-Arthur protocol where the verifier is a polynomial-size stoquastic quantum circuit: gates from {X, CX, CCX} with ancillae prepared in |0⟩ and |+⟩ states, with a final measurement in the Hadamard basis.

Merlin sends a polynomial-size proof such that:
1. If the answer is "yes," there exists a proof that Arthur accepts with probability at least α.
2. If the answer is "no," for all proofs Arthur accepts with probability at most β.

where 1/2 ≤ β < α ≤ 1 and α - β ≥ 1/poly(n).

The 2-local stoquastic Hamiltonian problem is StoqMA-complete. The transverse field Ising model is also StoqMA-complete.

There is no known strong error reduction for StoqMA; it is conjectured that StoqMA with strong error reduction is equivalent to {lang:MA}.

name: TALLY
desc:
Tally Languages. The class of decision problems for which every "yes" instance has the form 0^n (i.e., inputs are in unary). If TALLY intersects NPC (the NP-complete problems), then P = NP {ref:mah82}.

Contained in {lang:SPARSE}.

name: TC
desc:
Threshold Circuits. TC^i is the class of decision problems solvable by polynomial-size, depth O(log^i n) circuits with unbounded fanin AND, OR, and majority (MAJ) gates. A majority gate returns 1 if at least half of its inputs are 1. Other equivalent gate types include threshold gates (THR) and MOD_{p_n} where p_n is the n-th prime.

A uniformity requirement is sometimes also placed.

Each TC^i contains AC^i (in fact ACC^i) and is contained in NC^{i+1}. Thus NC = AC = TC.

name: TC^0
desc:
Constant-Depth Threshold Circuits. See {lang:TC} for the definition.

Contains {lang:ACC^0} and is contained in {lang:NC^1}.

TC^0 circuits of depth 3 are strictly more powerful than depth 2 {ref:hmp93}.

TC^0 circuits of depth 3 and quasipolynomial size can simulate all of {lang:ACC^0} {ref:yao90}.

There is a function in AC^0 whose computation with TC^0 depth-2 circuits requires exponentially many gates {ref:she08}.

A candidate pseudorandom function family computable in TC^0 exists under a subexponential lower bound on factoring {ref:nr97} {ref:nrr01}. Under this assumption, there is no natural proof separating TC^0 from P/poly {ref:rr97}.

The permanent of a 0-1 matrix cannot be computed in uniform TC^0 {ref:all99}.

Integer division is in U_D-uniform TC^0 and is complete for this class under AC^0 reductions {ref:hes01}.

name: TC^0(FOLL)
desc: The class of decision problems that are reducible to FOLL languages under TC^0-computable Turing reductions.

name: TC^1
desc:
Log-Depth Threshold Circuits. See {lang:TC} for the definition.

Also equivalent to the arithmetic/counting analogue of AC^1 modulo p_n (the n-th prime) {ref:rt92}.

name: TI
desc:
Tensor Isomorphism. The class of problems polynomial-time Turing reducible to Tensor Isomorphism. Defined in {ref:gq19}.

The relationship between TI over different fields is an open question, but many reductions hold over any field.

Over any field F, TI contains GI. Tensor Isomorphism itself (over finite fields) is in NP and coAM (and in fact SZK; the same holds over arbitrary fields in the BSS model). So if Tensor Isomorphism is NP-complete, PH collapses.

Many natural problems are TI-complete, such as isomorphism of algebras and modules.

name: TOWER
desc:
Iterated Exponential Time. Defined in {ref:sch16} as the union of DTIME(F_3(p(n))) over all elementary functions p(n), where F_3 is the third level of the fast-growing hierarchy (the iterated exponential function).

Strictly contains {lang:ELEMENTARY} and is strictly contained in {lang:PR}. Note that the same class is obtained if DTIME is replaced by NTIME or DSPACE.

Unlike ELEMENTARY and PR, which have no complete problems, TOWER has natural complete problems under elementary reductions: Star-Free Expression Equivalence (SFEq) and the satisfiability of Weak Monadic Theory of One Successor (WS1S).

name: TREE-REGULAR
desc: Same as REG, except that now the inputs are trees (say, binary trees) instead of strings.

name: TreeBQP
desc:
BQP Restricted to Tree States. The class of languages accepted by a BQP machine subject to the constraint that at every time step t, the machine's state is exponentially close to a tree state — a state expressible by a polynomial-size tree of additions and tensor products (together with complex constants and |0⟩ and |1⟩ leaf nodes).

More formally: a uniform classical poly-time algorithm generates a sequence of quantum gates and measurements. The measurement must accept with probability ≥ 2/3 for yes instances and ≤ 1/3 for no instances. If at any intermediate step the state is more than 2^{-Ω(n)} away from the nearest tree state of polynomial tree size, the outcome is chosen adversarially.

Contains {lang:BPP} and is contained in {lang:BQP}.

Defined in {ref:aar03b}, where it was also shown that TreeBQP is contained in the third level of PH, providing weak evidence that TreeBQP ≠ BQP.

name: UAP
desc: Same as AP, except we are promised that each existential quantifier has at most one 'yes' path, and each universal quantifier has at most one 'no' path.

name: UCFL
desc: The class of context-free languages which can be represented by grammars where each word in the language has exactly one leftmost derivation.

name: UE
desc: Has the same relation to E as UP does to P.

name: UL
desc: Has the same relation to L as UP does to P.

name: UL/poly
desc: Has the same relation to UL as P/poly does to P.

name: UP
desc:
Unambiguous Polynomial-Time. The class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine such that:
1. If the answer is "yes," exactly one computation path accepts.
2. If the answer is "no," all computation paths reject.

Defined in {ref:val76}.

"Worst-case" one-way functions exist if and only if P ≠ UP {ref:gs88} {ref:ko85}. "Worst-case" one-way permutations exist if and only if P ≠ UP ∩ coUP {ref:ht03}. (These are weaker than cryptographically useful one-way functions/permutations.)

There exists an oracle relative to which P ⊊ UP ⊊ NP {ref:rac82}, and these classes are distinct with probability 1 relative to a random oracle.

name: US
desc:
Unique Polynomial-Time. The class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine such that the answer is "yes" if and only if exactly one computation path accepts.

In contrast to {lang:UP}, a US machine can have more than one accepting path — that just means the input is not in the language.

Defined in {ref:bg82}. Contains coNP.

name: VC_k
desc:
Verification Class with a Circuit of Depth k:
- VC_0 is the class of compressible languages.
- VC_1 is the class of languages with local verification: they can be verified by testing only a small part of the instance (polynomial in witness length and log of instance length).
- VC_k for k ≥ 2 is the class of languages verifiable by a circuit of depth k, with size polynomial in witness length and instance length.

VC_0 ⊆ VC_or ⊆ VC_1 ⊆ VC_2 ⊆ VC_3 ⊆ ...

Introduced in {ref:hn06}; see there for formal definitions.

name: VC_or
desc:
Verification Class with OR. The class of languages that have verification presentable as the OR of m instances of SAT, each of size n (where m is the witness length and n is the instance length).

VC_0 ⊆ VC_or ⊆ VC_1. See {lang:VC_k} for context. Introduced in {ref:hn06}.

name: VPL
desc:
Visibly Pushdown Languages. The class of problems decidable by a visibly pushdown automaton. In a visibly pushdown automaton, all push and pop transitions must be triggered by special alphabet symbols (thus "visible" in the input word). Nondeterminism does not add expressive power, and VPL is closed under all Boolean operations.

Properly contains {lang:REG}. Properly contained in {lang:DCFL}.

Originated in {ref:am04}. See also {ref:am09}.

name: WAPP
desc:
Weak Almost-Wide PP. The class of decision problems for which there exists a #P function f, a polynomial p, and an ε > 0, such that for all inputs x:
1. If the answer is "yes," then 2^{p(|x|)} ≥ f(x) > (1+ε)·2^{p(|x|)-1}.
2. If the answer is "no," then 0 ≤ f(x) < (1-ε)·2^{p(|x|)-1}.

Defined in {ref:bgm02}, where it was also shown that WAPP is contained in {lang:AWPP} and {lang:SBP}.

name: WLC0
desc:
Unbounded Fanin Linear-Size Constant-Depth Circuits. The class of decision problems solvable by a nonuniform family of Boolean circuits with a linear number of wires, constant depth, and unbounded fanin.

Contained in LC^0, and therefore strictly contained in AC^0.

name: WPP
desc:
Wide PP. The class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine such that:
1. If the answer is "no," the number of accepting paths equals the number of rejecting paths.
2. If the answer is "yes," their difference equals a function f(x) computable in polynomial time (FP).

Defined in {ref:ffk94}.

Contained in C_=P ∩ coC_=P, and in {lang:AWPP}. Contains {lang:SPP} and {lang:LWPP}.

name: XNLP
desc: The class of decision problems of the form (x,k) (k a parameter) that are solvable in space O(f(k) log(n)) and time O(f(k) n^c), by a nondeterministic Turing machine, for some function f.

name: XOR-MIP*[2,1]
desc: Same as mipstar|MIP*[2,1], but with the further restriction that both provers send only a single bit to the verifier, and the verifier's output is a function of the exclusive-OR of those bits.

name: XP_uniform
desc: Same as XP except that the algorithm used must be the same for each k (though it can take k as input).

name: YACC
desc: A term of derision, used against a complexity class.

name: YP
desc: The class of decision problems for which there exists a polynomial-time machine M such that:

name: YPP
desc: The probabilistic analogue of YP; it is to YP what MA is to NP.

name: YP*
desc: YP except the advice string s_n can be verified in polynomial time without needing the input x {ref:ad14}.

name: YQP
desc: Is to YPP as BQP is to BPP, and QMA is to MA.

name: YQP*
desc: Is to YQP as YP* is to YP {ref:ad14}.

name: YQP*/poly
desc: Equal to BQP/qpoly {ref:ad14}.

name: ZBQP
desc:
Strict Quantum ZPP. Defined as RBQP ∩ coRBQP. Equivalently, the class of problems in NP ∩ coNP such that both positive and negative witnesses are in FBQP.

For example, square-free numbers are in ZBQP, because factoring is in FBQP and a factorization certifies a square divisor — certified in P via AKS primality {ref:aks02}.

Unlike EQP or ZQP, ZBQP would generalize ZPP in practice if quantum computers existed, in the sense that it provides proven answers. ZBQP^{ZBQP} = ZBQP.

Contains ZPP. Contained in RBQP and ZQP.

name: ZK
desc: Often used as a shorthand for (computational zero-knowledge) CZK, but may also be used as a general paradigm encomposing various classes ranging from perfect and statistical zero-knowledge (SZK) to computational ones (CZK), and also various forms of non-interactive zero-knowledge proof systems.

name: ZPE
desc: Same as ZPP, but with 2^O(n)-time instead of polynomial-time.

name: ZPL
desc:
Zero-Error Probabilistic Logspace. The logspace analog of ZPP: problems solvable by a probabilistic Turing machine with logarithmic space, zero error (always returns the correct answer), and termination probability 1 on all inputs (with expected polynomial running time).

Equals RL ∩ coRL. Contained in SC.

name: ZPP
desc:
Zero-Error Probabilistic Polynomial-Time. Defined as RP ∩ coRP. Equivalently, the class of problems solvable by randomized algorithms that always return the correct answer and whose expected running time is polynomial {ref:gil77}.

Contains primality testing {ref:ss77} {ref:ah87}, though primality is now in P {ref:aks02}.

Unlike BPP and RP, it is not known whether ZPP = P requires proving superpolynomial circuit lower bounds {ref:ki02}.

name: ZP·L
desc:
Zero-Error Probabilistic L with Two-Way Access to Randomness. Has the same relationship to {lang:BP·L} as ZPP has to BPP. Logspace polynomial-time Turing machine with a read-only randomness tape such that on input x:
1. With high probability, the machine correctly outputs whether x is in the language.
2. When the machine outputs "I don't know," it never outputs a wrong answer.

See {lang:BP·L} for context.

name: ZQP
desc:
Zero-Error Extension Of {lang:EQP}.
The class of questions that can be answered by a QTM that answers yes, no, or maybe. If the correct answer is yes, then P[no] = 0, and vice-versa; and the probability of maybe is at most 1/2. Since some of the probabilities have to vanish, ZQP has the same technical caveats as {lang:EQP}.
Defined independently in {ref:BW03} and in {ref:Nis02}. Equals {lang:RQP} ∩ {lang:coRQP}. There is an oracle such that ZQP^{ZQP} is larger than ZQP {ref:BW03}.

name: (M_k)P
desc:
Acceptance Mechanism by Monoid M_k. A monoid is a set with an associative operation and an identity element (like a group but without requiring inverses).

(M_k)P is the class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine where the i-th computation path outputs an element m_i of M_k, and the machine accepts iff m_1·m_2·...·m_s is the identity (where s is the number of paths).

Defined by {ref:her97}. For the special case where M is a group:
- If G is any nonsolvable group (e.g., S_5), then (G)P = PSPACE.
- (Z_k)P = coMod_kP, where Z_k is the cyclic group on k elements.
- If |G| = k, then (G)P contains coMod_kP.

name: (NP,P-samplable)
desc: See AvgP for basic notions of average-case complexity.

name: (NP ∩ coNP)/poly
desc: Together with NP/poly ∩ coNP/poly, has the same relation to NP ∩ coNP as P/poly has to P.

name: coAM
desc: Complement of {lang:AM}. The class of problems whose "no" instances have Arthur-Merlin proofs.

name: coC_=P
desc: Equals NQP {ref:fgh98}.

name: coMA
desc:
Complement of {lang:MA}. The class of problems whose "no" answers have Merlin-Arthur proofs.

coMA[1] = coMA (one-round coMA collapses to coMA) {ref:fgm89}. coAM ⊆ coMA since AM ⊆ MA is not trivially true but MA ⊆ AM implies coMA ⊇ coAM.

name: coNEXP
desc: Contained in NEXP/poly (folklore result reported in http://oldblog.computationalcomplexity.org/2004/01/little-theorem.html Fortnow's weblog).

name: coNL
desc: Complement of {lang:NL}. Equals NL by the Immerman-Szelepcsényi theorem {ref:imm88} {ref:sze87}.

name: coNP
desc:
Complement of NP. The class of decision problems whose "no" instances have polynomial-time checkable certificates (i.e., problems of the form "for all witnesses, ..."). Equivalently, problems whose complements are in NP.

If NP = coNP, then any inconsistent Boolean formula of size n has a proof of inconsistency of size polynomial in n. If NP ≠ coNP, then P ≠ NP (but the converse is not known).

Every problem in coNP has an IP interactive proof system {ref:sha92}.

name: coNPC
desc: The class of decision problems such that (1) they're in coNP and (2) every problem in coNP is reducible to them (under some notion of reduction).

name: coNP/poly
desc: If NP is contained in coNP/poly then PH collapses to S_2P^NP {ref:cch01}.

name: coNQP
desc: Complement of Nondeterministic Quantum Polynomial time, {lang:NQP}.

name: coRBQP
desc: Complement of {lang:RBQP}.

name: coRE
desc: Complement of Recursively enumerable languages, {lang:RE}. Languages whose rejection can be recognized by a Turing machine.

name: coRL
desc:
Complement of Randomized Logspace. The class of problems whose "no" instances have a randomized logspace algorithm (with one-sided error, no errors on "yes" instances).

Equals RL under the standard (one-sided error) definition. (Any randomized logspace algorithm for a language L can be adapted to recognize the complement.) See {lang:RL}.

name: coRNC
desc: Contains the problem of whether a bipartite graph has a perfect matching {ref:kar86}.

name: coRP
desc:
Complement of {lang:RP}. The class of problems solvable by a randomized polynomial-time algorithm with one-sided error: if the answer is "yes", the algorithm always accepts; if the answer is "no", the algorithm rejects with probability at least 1/2.

Contains primality testing {ref:ss77}. ZPP = RP ∩ coRP.

name: coRQP
desc: Complement of {lang:RQP}.

name: coUCC
desc: {ref:tor00} showed the following problem complete for coUCC under L reductions:

name: compIP
desc: Same as compNP but for interactive (IP) proofs instead of NP proofs.

name: compNP
desc: The class of decision problems L in NP such that, if the answer is "yes," then a proof can be constructed in polynomial time given access only to an oracle for L.

name: cq-Σ_2
desc:
Classical-Quantum-Σ_2P. A bounded-error quantum generalization of Σ_2P in which the first proof is classical, the second proof is quantum, and the verifier is a quantum circuit.

Defined in {ref:gk14}. Complete problems include Quantum Succinct Set Cover, Quantum Irredundant, and cq-Σ_2-LH (a quantum generalization of the canonical Σ_2P-complete problem) {ref:gk14}.

name: δ-BPP
desc:
δ-Semi-Random BPP. Same as BPP, except that the random bit source is biased: each bit may depend arbitrarily on all previous bits, but the only promise is that each bit is 1 with probability in the range [δ, 1-δ] conditioned on all previous bits.

So 0-BPP = P and (1/2)-BPP = BPP. For any δ > 0, δ-BPP = BPP {ref:vv85} {ref:zuc91}.

name: δ-RP
desc: δ-Semi-Random RP. Same as {lang:delta-BPP}, but for RP instead of BPP. For any δ > 0, δ-RP = RP {ref:vv85}.

name: frIP
desc:
Function-Restricted IP Proof Systems. The class of problems L that have a decider: there exists a BPP machine D such that for all inputs x, (1) if the answer is "yes" then D^L(x) (D with oracle for L) accepts with probability ≥ 2/3, and (2) if the answer is "no" then D^A(x) accepts with probability ≤ 1/3 for all oracles A.

Contains {lang:compIP} {ref:bg94} and {lang:Check} {ref:bk89}. Contained in MIP = NEXP {ref:frs88}. Assuming NEE ⊄ BPEE, NP ∩ Coh is not contained in frIP {ref:bg94}.

name: k-BWBP
desc: Alternate name for k-PBP.

name: k-EQBP
desc:
Width-k Polynomial-Time Exact Quantum Branching Programs. See k-PBP for the definition of a classical branching program. A quantum branching program is the natural quantum generalization: we have a quantum state in a Hilbert space of dimension k. Each step t consists of applying a unitary matrix U^(t)(x_i) depending on a single bit x_i of the input (these are the quantum analogues of "oblivious" branching programs). In the end we measure to decide whether to accept; there must be zero probability of error.

Defined in {ref:amp02}, where it was also shown that NC^1 is contained in 2-EQBP.

name: mAL
desc: Defined in {ref:gs90}. Equals mP by definition.

name: mL
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone log-width polynomial-size leveled circuits.

name: mNC^1
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone NC^1 circuits (i.e.

name: mNL
desc: See mP for the definition of a monotone nondeterministic Turing machine, due to {ref:gs90}.

name: mNP
desc: The class of decision problems for which a 'yes' answer can be verified in mP (that is, monotone polynomial-time).

name: mP
desc: The definition of this class, due to {ref:gs90}, is not obvious.

name: mP/poly
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a nonuniform family of polynomial-size Boolean circuits with only AND and OR gates, no NOT gates.

name: mTC^0
desc: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone TC^0 circuits (i.e.

name: mcoNL
desc: Defined in {ref:gs90}, where it was also shown that mcoNL does not equal mNL.

name: naCQP
desc: Defined in the conference version of {ref:abfl14}.

name: nuACC^0
desc: {lang:ACC^0} but with no uniformity condition.

name: para-P
desc: para-P is a less common name for FPT, but in line with other para- classes naming conventions.

name: polyL
desc: Equals DSPACE((log n)^c).

name: qq-QAM
desc: Same as QAM except Arthur sends Merlin polynomially many halves of EPR-pairs instead of random coinflips.

name: symP
desc: Alternate name for {lang:S_2P}.

name: FPT
desc: Fixed Parameter Tractable. Languages (x,k) with a deterministic algorithm running in time n^{O(1)}*f(k).

name: Kernel
desc: Problems that admit kernelization: languages (x,k) for which there is a _kernelization algorithm_ that processes the original instance in time poly(n,k) = (n+k)^{O(1)}, and produces an output string K of size f(k) for a computable function f, so that the original instance can be decided by running some (computable) algorithm on K. See [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernelization#Downey%E2%80%93Fellows_notation) for more details. This is a stronger requirement than being FPT, by essentially saying that the "slow" part of the algorithm that depends on k shouldn't need the whole input.

name: W[1]
desc:
Weighted Analogue of NP. The class of decision problems of the form (x, k) (k a parameter), that are fixed-parameter reducible to:

**Weighted 3SAT**: Given a 3SAT formula, does it have a satisfying assignment of Hamming weight k?

A fixed-parameter reduction is a Turing reduction running in time f(k)·p(|x|) for arbitrary f and polynomial p, where all queried instances have parameter ≤ k.

Contains FPT. Defined in {ref:df99}. If FPT = W[1], then NP ⊆ DTIME(2^{o(n)}).

Generalizes to {lang:W[t]}.

name: W[2]
desc:
The t=2 case of {lang:W[t]}. See W[t] for the definition.

W^*[2] = W[2] {ref:dft96}.

name: W[P]
desc:
Weighted Circuit Satisfiability. The class of decision problems of the form (x, k) (k a parameter), fixed-parameter reducible to:

**Weighted Circuit-SAT**: Given a Boolean circuit C (with no restriction on depth), does C have a satisfying assignment of Hamming weight k?

See {lang:W[1]} for the definition of fixed-parameter reducibility. Defined in {ref:df99}.

Contains {lang:W[SAT]}. Compare with {lang:para-NP} and XP, which are also parameterized versions of nondeterminism.

name: W[SAT]
desc:
Weighted Satisfiability. The class of decision problems of the form (x, k) (k a parameter), fixed-parameter reducible to:

**Weighted SAT**: Given a Boolean formula F (with no restriction on depth), does F have a satisfying assignment of Hamming weight k?

See {lang:W[1]} for the definition of fixed-parameter reducibility. Defined in {ref:df99}.

Contains W[t] for every t, and is contained in {lang:W[P]}.

name: W[*]
desc: Union of W[t]'s. The union of {lang:W[t]} over all t. Contained in {lang:W[SAT]}.

name: W[t]
desc:
The class of decision problems of the form (x, k) (k a parameter), fixed-parameter reducible to:

**Weighted Weft-t Depth-h Circuit-SAT**: Given a Boolean circuit C with a mixture of fanin-2 and unbounded-fanin gates, where the number of unbounded-fanin gates on any path to the root is at most t, and the total depth (fanin-2 and unbounded-fanin) is at most h. Does C have a satisfying assignment of Hamming weight k?

See {lang:W[1]} for the definition of fixed-parameter reducibility. Defined in {ref:df99}.

Contained in {lang:W[SAT]} and in W^*[t]. Generalizes W[1] (t=1) and W[2] (t=2).

name: W^*[t]
desc:
Same as {lang:W[t]}, except that the circuit depth can depend on the parameter k rather than being a fixed constant. The number of unbounded-fanin gates along any path to the root is still at most t.

W^*[1] = W[1] {ref:dft96}. W^*[2] = W[2] {ref:df97}. The problem is open for larger t.

name: XL
desc: Slicewise Logspace. Languages (x,k) with a deterministic algorithm running in space f(k)*log(n).

name: XNL
desc: Slicewise Nondeterministic Logspace. Languages (x,k) with a nondeterministic algorithm running in space f(k)*log(n).

name: XNP
desc: Slicewise NP. Languages (x,k) with a nondeterministic algorithm running in time n^f(k). Equivalently, problems with witnesses of size n^{f(k)} with a polynomial-time verifier.

name: XP
desc: Slicewise Polynomial time. Languages (x,k) with a deterministic algorithm running in time n^f(k).

name: para-L
desc: Parameterized Logspace. Languages (x,k) with a deterministic algorithm running in space f(k)+O(log(n)).
notes: There's a wide variety more classes and discussions of these classes at: https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~malcin/book/parameterized-algorithms.pdf ; http://satsmt2013.ics.aalto.fi/slides/Szeider.pdf ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022000017300089 ; https://www.mdpi.com/1999-4893/12/9/188 ; http://www.tcs.uni-luebeck.de/downloads/mitarbeiter/tantau/2013-hannover.pdf ; https://www.zhb.uni-luebeck.de/epubs/ediss1780.pdf ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.06984.pdf

name: para-NL
desc: Parameterized Nondeterministic Logspace. Languages (x,k) with a nondeterministic algorithm running in space f(k)+O(log(n)).

name: para-NL[f log]
desc: Like para-NL, but where the number of nondeterministic branches is bounded by O(f(k) log(n)).

name: para-NP
desc: Parameterized NP. Languages (x,k) with a nondeterministic algorithm running in time f(k)*n^{O(1)}. Equivalently, problems with a deterministic polynomial-time verifier that take a problem and witness, and the witness is of size f(k)*n^{O(1)}. A classic example is k-coloring: it's in NP for any k, and fixing k at a low value (such as 3) leaves it difficult. Since k-coloring is atually para-NP-hard too, it's para-NP-complete. Compare with XNP, where the exponent of the machine is allowed to depend on k.

name: PromiseBPP
desc: Promise Bounded error Probabilistic Polynomial time. Problems with a probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine promised to have at least a 2/3 chance of a correct answer.

name: PromiseBQP
desc: Promise Bounded error Quantum Polynomial time. Like BQP, but with a promise on the acceptance probabilities

name: PromiseMA
desc: Promise Merlin Arthur. Like MA, but with a promise on the acceptance probabilities.

name: PromiseQCMA
desc: Promise Quantum-Classical Merlin Arthur. Like QCMA, but with a promise on the acceptance probabilities

name: PromiseQMA
desc: Promise Quantum Merlin Arthur. Like QMA, but with a promise on the acceptance probabilities

name: PromiseRP
desc: Promise Randomized Polynomial time. Problems with a probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine promised to have at least a 1/2 chance rejecting correctly (and that always accept).

name: DQC1S
desc: Sampling Deterministic Quantum Computing with 1 Clean Bit. Samples produced from a quantum computer initialized with one qubit in the zero state and everything else in the maximally mixed state. Sampling version of DQC1, see there for more.

name: IQP
desc:
Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-Time. The class of sampling problems solvable by quantum circuits where all gates commute (i.e., diagonal gates in the computational basis). These circuits can be thought of as "instantaneous" since all gates act simultaneously.

Sampling from IQP circuits is conjectured to be hard for classical computers. If a classical computer can efficiently sample from IQP circuits to within multiplicative error, then the polynomial hierarchy collapses.

Related to BosonSampling and other quantum advantage proposals.
